title: Almost-everywhere regularity of stationary integral varifolds

issues.location: sections/excess.tex (Low-frequency barrier, roughly lines 400-1100) and sections/contact.tex (contact measure and the recursion in ct:separated)
issues.description: This is a coverage caveat, not a defect. The heat-contact construction, the low-frequency barrier with its well mergers, and the large-node recursion of the separated estimate carry the new content of the signed-excess induction. I only skimmed them and did not verify them line by line. Every closing step built on them checked out. A gap there would be invisible to this audit.

issues.location: sections/excess.tex, Lemma ex:bands; sections/packing.tex, completion of proof of sx:signed
issues.description: The rate comparisons hold, but only asymptotically and far out. For Q=2 the bands need B_1 = exp_3(sqrt(log_3 T)), which beats F_2(T)^3 only once log_4 T exceeds about 4. The bound log B_1 >> b(a_0) needs log_4 T above about 16. That is consistent with the paper's 'T large' convention, so it is not a gap. It does mean the threshold T_0 is non-effective and astronomically large.
issues.evidence: 'B_1^{1/10} >> F_Q(T)^3, S_h(a_0)^{C_*} << B_1^{eps_0}' together with F_Q(T)=exp_{2Q}(sqrt(log_{2Q} T))

coverage: I read the introduction, the full signed-excess statement, and most of local.tex: monotonicity, curved horizontal first variation, the Jacobian and integer counts, the scalar potential lemma, scalar mass propagation (including the M_+ / M_- argument), and the configuration/moment lemma. The exponent ranges check out: p<2m/(m-2) gives beta<1/m. In excess.tex I read the selection and bottom boundary, the future-envelope lemma (the reset rule and the Z-spending contradiction), and the bands lemma. I hand-checked the iterated exp/log rate comparisons for Q=2. In packing.tex I read the whole section: witness scales (time-bin identity t=(a+log I)/2, the one-well reset/nonreset contradiction), the controlled-density fraction, the dyadic packing lemma (retrace and paying-generation argument, plus the parameter arithmetic S>LR_*, (1-zeta)^N), contact charging, and the final contradiction (e^{-F^2}, e^{-B^{1/8}} = o(e^{-2F})). In centering.tex I read the setup, the cone-support claim, the fit lemma statement and Allard-type tilt step, and the full failed-fit lemma. There I verified the physical-scale hypotheses for applying sx:signed (the kappa and sigma choices), the limit identities A'=2A-D+R and H'=2D via Gaussian/polynomial weight derivatives, RH>=D^2, the frequency inequality P'>=(n-1)(n-2P), the explicit lower bound P>=-(e^{2(t-t0)}-1)/8, and the variance/separation conclusion. In inward.tex I read the variables, the inward bootstrap (P<=-K exclusion, the P>T^2 blow-up, the moderate-frequency ODE), the vanishing-height finish (Hoelder with the L^{p*} moment), and the completion via the typical-point a.e. hypotheses and H^m << mu on the support. I also read the round-sphere cone corollary in full. I only skimmed the contact-measure construction (ct:contact, ct:localization), the large-node part of ct:separated, the barrier/merger proposition and initialization in excess.tex, the glued-center/weights propositions, and the collar and frequency lemmas in inward.tex.
main_claim: For every stationary integral m-varifold in an open subset of R^{m+n} (any m,n>=1, with no stability, density or codimension hypothesis), H^m(Sing V)=0. The proof shows that every point with tangent Q|P| and o(r^m) mass of multiplicity other than Q is regular, which covers the local criterion in BDD Conjecture 1.3. It rests on a signed-excess estimate, int w(2M-D-C_Q Lambda) <= e^{-F_Q(T)} d, proved by induction on Q. The same conclusion is derived on round spheres.
